reason: The blind-ended lymphatic capillaries appear suited to collecting excess fluid from the tissue spaces.
expectation: The capillaries will provide a route for excess tissue fluid to enter the lymphatic system.

effect: The tissue spaces now have lymphatic capillaries that take up fluid and proteins; the collecting vessels should extend that route.
reaction: The inward arrows make the capillaries' role clear.
reason: The collecting lymphatic vessels appear to be the next link in returning the collected fluid.
expectation: The collecting vessels will carry fluid onward from the lymphatic capillaries.

effect: The collecting vessels extend the lymphatic route, with muscle movement and valves helping lymph move forward. The return ducts are the next apparent connection.
reaction: The paired panels make the role of muscle movement and valves clear.
reason: The return ducts appear to connect the lymphatic pathways to the veins.
expectation: The ducts will complete a route for lymph to return to the blood.

effect: The lymphatic route now reaches veins near the neck. It still needs to be connected to the circulation and arm.
reaction: The completed route makes the return path clear.
reason: The arm needs to connect to the circulation for its muscles to receive oxygen and nutrients.
expectation: The arm's vessels will connect to the circulation, supplying its muscles.

alternatives.reason: The ducts also need to connect to the veins, but supplying the arm seems like a useful next step.

effect: The arm is now connected to the heart and lungs, and its tissue spaces still contain fluid and protein that need a return route.
reaction: The tissue inset clearly connects blood supply with the remaining drainage problem.
reason: The lymph drainage network appears to complete the return route from the supplied arm to the blood.
expectation: The lymphatic network will collect excess tissue fluid and return it to the bloodstream.

effect: The lymph drainage network is now connected to the supplied arm and circulation, completing the route for excess tissue fluid and proteins to return to the blood.
reaction: The final model brings the supply and drainage routes together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the lymphatic network to the supplied arm was most worthwhile because the final inset brings blood supply, tissue exchange and fluid return into one picture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the return ducts was fairly predictable after the collecting vessels, although it completed the route to the veins.

surprise.text: I was interested to learn that muscle movement can squeeze lymph onward and that lymph vessels can also contract.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each added a visible link in the supply or drainage route.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter if it used the assembled systems to explore a new situation. The connected final model was satisfying, though several assembly steps were predictable.
